subject: Computer Networking
title: Cloudflare's Regex Catastrophe (2019)
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Cloudflare's Regex Catastrophe (2019).

hook.text: On July 2, 2019, Cloudflare's CPUs spiked to 100% worldwide. Millions of websites returned errors.

buildup.text: A developer deployed a firewall rule with a regular expression that had catastrophic backtracking behavior.

discovery.text: The regex consumed all CPU on every edge server globally. No capacity remained to serve web traffic.

twist.text: The regex looked harmless in testing. Certain inputs caused exponential processing — a known regex pitfall.

climax.text: Cloudflare rolled back in 27 minutes and published a transparent post-mortem. They added regex time limits.

punchline.text: One regular expression melted a global CDN. Tiny code, huge impact.

quiz.question: What programming issue caused Cloudflare's 2019 outage?
options: A regex with catastrophic backtracking that consumed all CPU
A memory leak that filled all available RAM
A database query that locked all tables

details.summary: In July 2019, a regular expression deployed to Cloudflare's WAF caused CPU usage to spike to 100 percent across every server in every data center simultaneously. The outage lasted 27 minutes and affected millions of websites that use Cloudflare for protection and CDN services.
details.whyItMatters: A single poorly written regex brought down a service protecting millions of websites. It demonstrated how a tiny code change can have global impact in centralized infrastructure.
takeaways: One regex caused 100% CPU across all Cloudflare servers
The outage affected millions of websites for 27 minutes
Cloudflare added regex complexity limits after the incident

faq.question: How can a regular expression cause a global outage?
faq.answer: The regex contained a pattern that caused catastrophic backtracking. When the regex engine could not find a match, it explored exponentially many possibilities before giving up. The WAF rules ran on every request across all servers, so CPU consumption hit 100% globally.

faq.question: What did Cloudflare change after this incident?
faq.answer: They added automated regex complexity analysis to prevent deployment of backtracking-prone patterns. They also implemented staged rollouts for WAF rule changes and added CPU usage circuit breakers that automatically revert changes when consumption spikes.
